title: Bengal in talks to buy back Singur's 997 acres for industry; ₹205 crore relief for rain-hit farmers
dek: Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said the state is negotiating with farmers for the former Nano site, and announced compensation for about 5.7 lakh farmers hit by Cyclone Akvan's rain.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
West Bengal's government is negotiating with farmers to buy back the 997 acres at Singur in Hooghly district that were once meant for Tata Motors' Nano car factory, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said on Sunday, as he announced ₹205 crore in relief for about 5.7 lakh farmers whose crops were damaged by days of rain from Cyclone Akvan.

Speaking to reporters in Kolkata, Mr Adhikari said the West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation had been asked to acquire the Singur land and that negotiations with farmers were under way "to purchase the land at a reasonable rate", according to reports. He did not say which company would use it. On Saturday, Union Minister of State Sukanta Majumdar had said after Prime Minister Narendra Modi's programme at IIT Kharagpur that "Ashok Leyland is coming to Singur" to build a truck plant. Neither the company nor the state government has confirmed that.

## Crop relief

The relief package is based on a preliminary agriculture department report that puts the damaged farmland at about 1.6 lakh hectares, Mr Adhikari said, according to reports. Farmers will get ₹17,000 a hectare for crop loss and ₹22,500 a hectare for land that carries more than one crop. Farmers with damage on as little as one cottah of land will get at least ₹2,000, which he said was aimed at supporting small farmers. He told officials to speed up payments.

The worst-hit districts were Howrah, Hooghly, Bankura, Purba Bardhaman, North and South 24 Parganas, Jhargram, Purulia and parts of Purba Medinipur, according to reports. The rain damaged vegetables and standing aman paddy in south Bengal last week and pushed up vegetable prices in Kolkata markets.

## Singur, 20 years on

The Left Front government acquired about 997 acres at Singur in 2006 for the Nano plant. The acquisition led to a long farmers' protest led by Mamata Banerjee, then in opposition, and Tata Motors moved the project to Sanand in Gujarat in 2008. In August 2016 the Supreme Court quashed the acquisition and ordered the land returned to its owners. Much of that land has since stayed unused.

Mr Adhikari said farmers had not been able to grow paddy, potato or mustard on the returned land, that a fish-farming attempt by an earlier government had failed, and that farmers had already been compensated twice, once under the Left Front and again in 2016-17, according to reports. He said his government had accepted the 2013 land acquisition law and the idea of land pooling, without giving details.

The state also plans to buy land from owners of closed jute mills in the Barrackpore industrial belt, and is interested in land in Bhangar, near New Town, from owners willing to sell, he said. He said 8,000 to 10,000 acres would be acquired for industry over the next three months, and that the state was exploring solar power projects in Purulia.

## Other announcements

Mr Adhikari also announced plans for an administrative hub in New Town with new buildings for the state Assembly and the Calcutta High Court, an administrative complex and housing for judges, ministers and senior officials, according to reports. He said the Assembly building was being planned to allow for a possible increase in the number of seats from the present 294 to more than 400, and that the High Court's present building was short of space. No cost or timeline was given.

He said he would write to External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar about reported attacks on Hindus in Narail in Bangladesh, and would ask Union Home Minister Amit Shah to consider further relaxing rules under the Citizenship (Amendment) Act for people facing religious persecution in neighbouring countries, reports said.

Reports of the briefing did not carry a response from the Trinamool Congress, which led the original Singur movement and is now in opposition, or from the CPI(M).

## What happens next

The agriculture department is to finalise its damage survey before payments are made. Any purchase at Singur depends on agreement with thousands of individual landowners; the 2016 verdict returned land to 9,117 of them, according to reports.
